title: Forms and conditions

blocks.heading: Forms and conditions
blocks.text: Investment, grants, technical assistance, loans and credits have different ownership, repayment and delivery arrangements. A loan is a borrowing arrangement; debt is the amount outstanding. Emergency or development purpose differs from bilateral delivery between countries or multilateral delivery through institutions.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Direct investment and companies
blocks.text: Foreign direct investment can establish productive facilities and connect technology or markets through firms, including multinationals. Local skills, suppliers and retained benefits matter; finance and jobs can coexist with profits leaving or environmental costs.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Loans and credits
blocks.text: Foreign loans provide resources with repayment obligations, often with interest and agreed timing. They may finance useful capacity but create debt-service needs. Borrowing for an unusable asset adds obligations without the expected earning or service benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Assess the arrangement
blocks.text: An invented council compares a small grant for a limited service with an affordable loan that reaches more residents but commits later revenue. The grant protects future funds; the loan widens current reach. Neither financing label settles the judgement. Compare need, maintained operation, repayment capacity and the services postponed under each feasible option.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
